creator: Markiplier
move: Opens with an honest session contract: says he may not play the full game, then adds the clause that a game which captivates him changes that, setting expectations before any play
timing: Contract stated inside the first minute, before the first real decision
phrasing_shape: plain statement of limits, conditional promise, straight into play
aggregate_note: Up-front honesty about session scope is rarer in the Show lane, where premise is usually a promise of spectacle rather than a limit

creator: Markiplier
move: During a collapsing-room sequence relayed by his squad, commentary thins to short fragments and warnings while the game's own audio and the squad's reports carry the tension
timing: Talk density drops hard for the duration of the event, then rebuilds sentence by sentence as the room settles
phrasing_shape: broken short phrases, repeated warnings, long gaps left to game sound
aggregate_note: Deliberate thinning at dread peaks is the Coach lane pattern; Show-lane creators mostly fill the same moments

creator: Markiplier
move: Reads a full subject file attentively, treating the lore document as evidence about what happened to the crew, then releases the built-up dread with a small domestic joke
timing: Document gets unhurried time; the joke lands within seconds of the file ending, resetting the temperature
phrasing_shape: careful reading voice, brief verdict, throwaway joke as pressure valve
aggregate_note: Forensic patience with lore plus a joke valve recurs in the investigator-style creators sampled so far

creator: Markiplier
move: Manages a fear spike with a repeated self-instruction not to look to either side, turning the refusal to look into the beat itself while he works the console
timing: The repetition runs for roughly twenty seconds against rising game cues, then breaks into action
phrasing_shape: same short refusal repeated with rising strain, no punchline until the moment passes
aggregate_note: Fear shown through a verbal ritual rather than volume is distinctive; most sampled creators escalate loudness at this trigger instead

creator: Markiplier
move: An escape attempt collapses into a jump scare: one full scream, then within seconds a self-interested joke about abandoning the team, and baseline commentary is restored almost immediately
timing: Peak lasts a few seconds; recovery to ordinary analytic voice inside roughly ten seconds
phrasing_shape: scream, sheepish aside, joke at his own expense, back to business
aggregate_note: High peak with very fast decay is the reactor signature this lane was sampled for; the joke is the brake pedal

creator: Markiplier
move: Cornered by a creature, he screams, then immediately narrates his own decision psychology, explaining that a cornered animal chooses to fight and that he chose it
timing: Self-analysis starts within about five seconds of the scream, while the danger is still on screen
phrasing_shape: scream, breath, first-person post-mortem delivered in present tense
aggregate_note: Naming the internal state instantly after a peak recurs across his sampled peaks and separates him from pure-volume reactors

creator: Markiplier
move: The loudest peak of the video is frustration, not fear: a forced decommission choice makes him openly angry, he converts it into a comedy argument with the game character demanding a manager, and at the close he does the arithmetic of the ending he missed and delivers a balanced verdict on the game
timing: Anger vents for under a minute before the bit takes over; the forensic breakdown waits for the ending and runs unhurried
phrasing_shape: open venting, absurd escalation of the complaint into roleplay, then calm numbers and a two-sided review
aggregate_note: Frustration out-peaking fear, then converting to analysis, is a strong individual signature; failure as material rather than payoff matches the field

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Opens at full volume with his greeting ritual, then immediately apologises to the audience for the gap since Part 1, acknowledging that viewers demanded more of the series and that life got in the way
timing: Accountability beat occupies the first half minute before any gameplay
phrasing_shape: maximum-energy greeting, abrupt drop into sincere apology, intimate lock-in with the viewer
aggregate_note: Series accountability as an opening move is unique in the current sample; Show-lane openings sell premise, this one services a relationship

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Admits within minutes that he has forgotten how to play after two weeks away, plays his own shame as a bit, and voices real frustration at himself while relearning the controls live
timing: Not-knowing is declared immediately, not covered; the relearning struggle recurs openly all video
phrasing_shape: confession, self-mockery, muttered problem-solving, volume spike when it clicks
aggregate_note: Open not-knowing as entertainment matches the field's uncertainty-honesty pattern, but the shame-as-bit framing is his own

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Escalates a minor economy discovery, a customer quietly slipping him extra money, into a full theatrical bit about bribery and easy profit
timing: Peak arrives instantly over a small event and holds while he milks it, then drops when the next task starts
phrasing_shape: incredulous question repeated, mock-scandal tone, greed played as celebration
aggregate_note: Low escalation threshold over trivial stakes contrasts directly with the rationed escalation in the other half of this pair

creator: jacksepticeye
move: A repair job triggers a long genuine-wonder tangent about a classic portable music player: its design, how impossible a pristine one is to find, and a direct appeal to viewers who might own one
timing: Tangent runs for minutes mid-grind without apology, then folds back into the repair
phrasing_shape: admiration stated plainly, personal history, rhetorical questions about the designers, audience appeal
aggregate_note: Wonder as downtime fuel generalises across the Coach lane; here it is personal nostalgia rather than game systems

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Through a long fiddly reassembly he vents continuously, apologises to the audience for how painful his disorganisation is to watch, and still grinds the job to completion before declaring he never wants to build one again
timing: Frustration is sustained across the whole task rather than spiking; completion, not a reset, ends it
phrasing_shape: running complaint, self-aware apology, small victories announced, exhausted verdict
aggregate_note: Persistence through voiced misery is the enthusiast pattern; the audience apology inside the struggle is a relationship move worth tagging

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Produces a full scream over a missing shop item while restocking parts, peak amplitude spent on a completely trivial stake, then returns to business inside a few seconds
timing: Scream is instant, decay is instant; the next mundane line gets ordinary full energy
phrasing_shape: building rhetorical question at rising volume, scream, immediate reset to chat
aggregate_note: Peak amplitude decoupled from stake size is the clearest calibration contrast in this pair and a warning against copying amplitude without threshold

creator: jacksepticeye
move: Ends the session on his own fatigue rather than a game peak: says plainly that the repetition has tired his brain, thanks viewers, and asks for their thoughts and feelings in the comments
timing: Close is unhurried and warm, no recap or highlight reel
phrasing_shape: honest limit stated, gratitude, open-ended questions handed to the audience
aggregate_note: Ending on the performer's state instead of the game's biggest moment is unusual in the sample and reads as long-series confidence
